inspectedCaptures.inspection: Shared busy controls remain visible with the reduced-motion preference. Motion and action behavior are verified by the browser case.
Revealed composer retains the exact draft and existing tile arrangement.
Native phone composition retains static busy controls. The fixture contribution toolbar remains crowded; no visual redesign is claimed.
Short phone viewport keeps the composer, model and attachment controls, and cancellation action visible.

verifiedBehaviors: Committed canonical agent updates apply without conversation resets on desktop and phone.
Core and plugin gap recovery converge; plugin paging survives recovery.
Real core and plugin document hide/restore retains content, draft, scroll, and expansion within the same document.
A-B-A navigation retains draft, file actions and context; optional enrichment and PR feedback stay panel-local.
Saved arrangements with identical panel inventories restore correctly; departed Dockview owners release and drafts survive return and responsive changes.
Hidden Changes updates retain the row anchor; visible unfocused updates preserve the reader and editor focus.
Optional Monaco loads on desktop first use; the phone native viewer opens without loading Monaco.
Normal/reduced motion and CSS fallback preserve visible status and usable plugin actions.
Desktop hover, keyboard, permissions, attachments, cancellation and disclosure keep the active composer usable.
Native phone touch, long questions, short viewports and single-chat navigation retain their input controls and drafts.
limits: The 50 cases are targeted correctness gates, not the full repository E2E suite.
The Dockview stream regression uses a two-second correctness window; full 60-second dense comparisons remain separate.
Passing correctness does not resolve the scripted control wheel failure or candidate frame-gap regressions.
The earlier unexplained phone deep-tree failure remains historical evidence. A passing final run does not establish its original cause.
No M2 Air, field INP, battery, total-process availability, or leak claim follows.
